thread:
Lee: Quick sync: noticed cluster-autoscaler is removing GPU nodes with pods that take ~10m to come back. This is hitting inference jobs. Proposing a safe-drain playbook + small CA tweak. Thoughts?

Carmen: Which pool/region? can you paste the CA log snippet?

Lee: us-west1-gpu-pool, node gke-gpu-9f4.
CA log:
```
I0505 14:22:01.123 scale_down.go: CA: Node gke-gpu-9f4 is underutilized (util 0.08), will try to drain
I0505 14:22:10.456 evict.go: Pod inference-prod-0 can't be evicted: pod disruption budget
```

Aditya: PDBs can block evictions; CA should skip nodes if pods are non-evictable. But if pods eventually become evictable, CA will retry and drain.

Mira: We've used a high PriorityClass for trainers to avoid preemption; that doesn't stop CA. Two quick options: annotate pods with `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=false` or lower scaleDownUtilizationThreshold for GPU pools.

Jen: :thumbsup: Can we add a pre-drain hook that checks for active CUDA jobs and delays drain by adding a temporary taint instead of immediate eviction?

Carmen: I'll sketch a small playbook. Steps:
1) cordon node
2) run a check script that queries pods on node for long-running GPU jobs
3) if safe, apply `kubectl drain` with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300` and `--timeout=15m`
4) if not safe, label node `no-scale-down=true` and uncordon

Lee: Example commands and snippets:
```
# cordon
kubectl cordon gke-gpu-9f4
# list pods on node
kubectl get pods --all-namespaces --field-selector spec.nodeName=gke-gpu-9f4 -o wide
# drain (careful)
kubectl drain gke-gpu-9f4 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300 --timeout=15m
```
PriorityClass sample:
```
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: gpu-protected
value: 500000
globalDefault: false
description: "High priority to reduce preemption for long gpu jobs"
```
PDB example to allow 1 eviction only:
```
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: inference-pdb
spec:
  maxUnavailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: inference
```

sre-oncall-bot: autoscaler: scale down event suppressed for node gke-gpu-9f4 (pods non-evictable)

Aditya: For CA flags we should set for gpu pool:
`--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.4` and `--scale-down-unneeded-time=20m` plus `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` as needed.

Mira: Also consider setting node annotation `cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/scale-down-disabled` on nodes we want to protect while jobs run. We'll add a small operator to flip it during job start/end.

Jen: Ops, can you add this to runbooks and open a follow-up to tweak CA for us-west1-gpu-pool? I'll volunteer to test.

Lee: Thanks — I'll open an ops-runbooks PR with the playbook and a ticket to change CA flags for gpu pools. We'll also add the pre-drain check as a small Kubernetes Job. /cc @Aditya @Mira
